summary: Paul Williams studied at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he held posts at Wadham College and the University of Bristol (~1980–2011) and was president of the UKABS.

Paul de Lagarde was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Rückert and at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula Arai works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Waseda, Kalamazoo, and Harvard under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith, she has held posts at Vanderbilt (1994–2002), LSU, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio, later serving in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), the Congregation of the Index, and the Pontifical Urban University.

Pavankumar Satuluri is a scholar in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He has held academic posts at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (attested 2024–2025).

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Yangon, University of Calcutta, and University of Oxford, and later served as professor and principal at Yangon, principal at the University of Adult Education, and Burma Historical Commission chairman.
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at UCLA in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum, having also studied under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Peipei Qiu specializes in Japanology and Sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where she completed her doctorate under Donald Keene and also studied under Paul Rouzer, before taking up a post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

Pema Bhum is a scholar of Tibetology. He previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and directed the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön works in Buddhist studies. She was educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley, studied under Chime Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Chögyam Trungpa, and Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and served as director of Boulder Shambhala Center and abbess of Gampo Abbey.
Pema Donyo Nyinje is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973), and taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin was a Tibetan scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Namgyel studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Pema Sherpa is a doctoral candidate in religious studies at McMaster University (attested 2026), where she works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Pema Tsering, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied under Shenphen Nangwa, taught Ruth Gamble, and held a post at the University of Bonn (attested 1996).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught Terton Sogyal and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Pema Wangchok Gyelpo was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Mipam Gyatso, and Khakyab Dorje, among others, and taught disciples including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
